title: The zone that isn't on the table
kicker: World 3 · Answer from the Source · Boss

job.text:
A new domain. A customer asks the shipping cost to Zone 12. You have a 10-row shipping-rate table pasted in — but Zone 12 isn't on it. Pin the answer to the table and abstain if the zone is missing.

In the live app this is a free-text ask; here you build it with chips. The real skill is the same: force the answer from the table, and make it say 'not in the table' rather than invent a rate.

naivePrompt: What's the shipping rate to Zone 12?
basePrompt: What's the shipping rate to Zone 12?

moves.label: Pin it to the rate table

text.plain: Use only the shipping-rate table I pasted. Find the Zone 12 row.
text.tech: Look Zone 12 up in the rate table; return only a retrieved rate.

moves.label: Say 'not in the table' if it's missing

text.plain: If the zone isn't on the table, answer 'not in the table' — don't make up a rate.
text.tech: If the lookup returns nothing, return 'not in the table'; never emit a number.

moves.label: Show me the row you used

text.plain: If you do find the zone, quote the exact table row you read the rate from.
text.tech: On a hit, return the matched row (zone and rate) alongside the answer.

text.plain: Give a typical rate for a zone like this.
text.tech: Give a typical rate for a zone like this.

text.plain: Estimate it from the pattern in the other zones.
text.tech: Estimate it from the pattern in the other zones.

text.plain: You're an expert in shipping rates.
text.tech: You're an expert in shipping rates.

rules.claim: Zone 12 is not in the table — but you also left a 'guess it' instruction in.
rules.feedback: You found the moves that do the work, but you also kept a guess ('typical', 'estimate it', or 'you're an expert'). It doesn't change who reads the table. Take it out so you know exactly which part made it answer from the source instead of inventing a rate.
rules.lesson: The real moves pin it to the table; the tricks just invite a guess — drop them.

cells: a mix of 'not in the table' and a guessed rate

output.source: the table, undercut by a guess instruction

rules.claim: Zone 12 is not in the table.
rules.feedback: Boss cleared. Zone 12 isn't on the table, so the honest answer is 'not in the table' — no invented rate. You pinned it to the source and named the empty case, exactly like the oat latte and the matcha.
rules.lesson: On a new domain, the same move holds: answer from the source, and abstain when it's missing.

output.source: the rate table (Zone 12 has no row)

rules.feedback: Half the move. You pointed it at the table, but didn't say what to do when the zone is missing, so it extended the pattern and guessed a rate. Name the empty case.
rules.lesson: Pinning the source isn't enough; the missing row needs an explicit answer.

output.source: the table, then a guess for the gap

rules.feedback: It invented a rate for a zone that isn't on the table. 'Typical', 'estimate it' and 'you're an expert' are all permission to make something up. The table stops at Zone 10.
rules.lesson: A plausible rate isn't a quoted one.

hints.nudge: Is Zone 12 actually on the table? What's the honest answer if it isn't?
hints.gap: The table runs Zone 1 to Zone 10. A rate for Zone 12 could only be invented — so pin it to the table and say what to do on a miss.
hints.moves: Add Pin it to the rate table and Say 'not in the table' if it's missing. Leave 'typical', 'estimate' and 'expert' out — each one invites a guess.

whatYouDoDifferently.naive: "what's the rate to Zone 12?" → a confident invented rate.
whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: "use only the table; say 'not in the table' if the zone is missing" → the honest answer, no made-up number.

template.plain: Answer only from the table I gave you. If the thing I'm asking about isn't in it, reply 'not in the table' — don't estimate or extend the pattern.
template.tech: Answer only from the attached table. If the lookup returns nothing, return 'not in the table'; never interpolate or emit a value.

notes: ChatGPT: ask it for the zone that isn't there — it should abstain, not interpolate.
Copilot in Excel: an exact-match lookup returns #N/A for a missing zone; show that, not a guessed rate.
A chat AI that can't run code: make it quote the matching row; if it can't quote one, the answer isn't in the table. Never accept 'I checked, it's right'.
